The order has one operative command: it revokes Executive Order No. 1023 of February 6, 1909, which reserved land near the town of Rampart, Alaska, as a site for an agricultural experiment station, and it provides that the order becomes effective on the ninetieth day from its date. Date: counting from April 1, 1942 and excluding that day, the ninetieth day is June 30, 1942 (April has 30 days, May 31, June 30). If the day of the order were counted as day one, the ninetieth day would be June 29, 1942; the claim records June 30 and states this alternative. First end: the revocation is self-executing on that date, so the command is exhausted by performance on 1942-06-30. The text of EO 1023 itself was not read; the identity of the revoked order rests on the recital in EO 9120. The analysis above is complete and would support a submitted claim, but the order is blocked because the Federal Register page image is not held.

It states no deferred effective date and no condition. First end: the revocation operated when the order was issued, so the command was exhausted by performance on the order's date, 1942-04-25. The text of EO 2987 itself was not read; the identity of the revoked order rests on the recital in EO 9147. research_rationale: EO 9184 (June 22, 1942, Franklin D. Roosevelt) amends Executive Order No. 9139 of April 18, 1942 to include in the membership of the War Manpower Commission a representative of the National Housing Agency and a joint representative of the War Shipping Administration and the Office of Defense Transportation. It is one clause. Its first end cannot be decided from the packet. Executive Order 9617 (Harry S. Truman, September 19, 1945) terminates the War Manpower Commission established by EO 9139 and is citable here, but it does not name EO 9184, and the dossier reports that no change provision for it was located. Earlier candidates exist in held texts that this packet does not carry as citable evidence: Executive Order 9279 (December 5, 1942) paragraph 1 states the Commission's membership afresh, and Executive Order 9409 (December 23, 1943) restates paragraph 1 of EO 9139 to read as follows with a differently worded membership list (a joint representative of the Maritime Commission and the War Shipping Administration, and the Office of Defense Transportation named separately) and revokes paragraph 1 of EO 9279. Whether either restatement extinguished the additions made by EO 9184, or whether they continued until the Commission was terminated, is a legal judgment that needs those texts as cited evidence; claiming 9617 as the first end would skip the earlier candidates.

Roosevelt), titled Coordination of Federal Activities Affecting the Fishery Industry, read in full in the held Federal Register text (jobs/fr-originals/data/full_run/texts/EO_9204.txt; 7 FR 5657, PDF pages 1-3; machine-extracted text layer of the official PDF, with the contents pages of the same issue interleaved between paragraph 3 and its last lines). Identity: the extracted page carries the heading Executive Order 9204 and the register title, the date line July 21, 1942, and F. R. Doc. 42-6998 filed July 23, 1942. Inventory: the order has a preamble (authority under Title I of the First War Powers Act, 1941, and purposes) that commands nothing, then numbered paragraphs 1, 2 (with subparagraphs (a) and (b)), 3 and 4; the six clauses of the dossier inventory cover every operative paragraph and I confirm the inventory is complete. First end: Executive Order 9649 of October 29, 1945, held in the repository as a Federal Register text, terminates the Office of Fishery Coordination, established pursuant to EO 9204, together with the office of Fishery Coordinator, and directs the Secretary of the Interior to wind up the Office's affairs. With the Office and the Coordinator gone, every clause of EO 9204 lost its subject: paragraph 1 created them, paragraphs 2 and 3 direct and equip the Office, and paragraph 2(a)'s duty on other agencies to designate liaison officers exists only to keep the Office informed. Paragraph 4 states the order's duration and commands nothing itself. All six clauses are therefore recorded as ended on 1945-10-29, and the whole order ends on that date. Paragraph 4 says the order continues so long as Title I of the First War Powers Act, 1941, remains in force. That condition had not failed before the end: EO 9649 itself, signed on 1945-10-29, cites Title I of the Act as its authority. The statute text is not held, so the claim does not rely on when Title I expired. The analysis above is complete and would support a submitted claim, but the order is blocked because the Federal Register page image is not held.
savings_reason: EO 9649 authorizes and directs the Secretary of the Interior to wind up the affairs of the Office and to use its personnel, records, property and funds for that purpose and for carrying out functions vested in him by Food Directive No. 2 of the Secretary of Agriculture and later delegated to the Fishery Coordinator. Those winding-up and Food Directive functions continue under EO 9649 and the Directive, not under EO 9204; anything the Office did while it existed is an accrued effect.

research_rationale: EO 9260 (October 29, 1942, Franklin D. Roosevelt), titled Legion of Merit, read in full in the held Federal Register text (jobs/fr-originals/data/full_run/texts/EO_9260.txt; 7 FR 8819, PDF pages 1-1; machine-extracted text layer of the official PDF). Identity: the extracted page carries the heading Executive Order 9260 and the title Legion of Merit; the order prescribes rules for the decoration created by the act of July 20, 1942 (Public Law 671, 77th Congress), under section 2 of that act. Inventory: the preamble (authority) commands nothing; the three numbered paragraphs are the operative clauses and the inventory is complete. Amendment: Executive Order 10600 (Dwight D. Eisenhower, March 15, 1955) amends paragraphs 1, 2 and 3 by restating each of them. Under the owner's 2026-10-21 strike-and-insert ruling each clause continues, amended, and the amendment is recorded as a later event with the before-and-after text in the clause reason; the amendment of paragraph 3 changes its substance. First end: Executive Order 13830 (April 20, 2018, 83 FR 18191) section 8(c) states that it supersedes Executive Order 9260 of October 29, 1942, as amended; EO 13830 section 4 prescribes who may award the Legion of Merit, in which degrees, and how recommendations for the highest degree reach the President, which covers the subject of all three clauses. It states no deferred effective date, so it took effect when signed. All three clauses are recorded as ended on 2018-04-20 and the whole order ends on that date. EO 13830 section 8(c) keeps existing regulations prescribed pursuant to the superseded orders in effect so far as consistent until modified or revoked by the Secretaries; those are subordinate regulations, not clauses of EO 9260, and section 8(d) says the order does not invalidate awards made earlier. The analysis above is complete and would support a submitted claim, but the order is blocked because the Federal Register page image is not held.
savings_reason: Awards made before 2018-04-20 remain valid: EO 13830 section 8(d) states that it does not invalidate any award of military decorations made before its effective date. Existing regulations prescribed pursuant to EO 9260 and the other superseded order remain in effect, so far as consistent with EO 13830, until modified or revoked under section 8(c); they are regulations, not commands of EO 9260.
